You can filter by folderId, name and type; when several are set, all must match, and name matching ignores case. tools.name: convertReport
tools.title: Convert report to slide deck
tools.description: Turns an older report of type GoogleSlides or MicrosoftPowerPoint, which updates a Google Slides presentation or a PowerPoint file in OneDrive or SharePoint, into a new report of type SlideDeck, as Convert to Rollstack slides in the app does. The new report gets the file's slides, and each sync that can be converted becomes a datasheet reading the same source, drawn by a tile where the sync's chart, table or picture was. The older report and its file stay as they are. The file is read with the older report's owner's account. Answers the new report and what became of each sync, with the reason for one not converted, such as a burst variant's (convert a whole burst with convertBurst) or one of a source with no datasheets: the conversion starts the new report's update to fill its charts, answered as runId: follow it with getReportRun, or start one with startReportRun when runId is null. Only the older report's editors may. It answers once the conversion ends, which can take a few minutes for a large report: send an Idempotency-Key (MCP: idempotencyKey) so a retry doesn't convert it twice. Counts against the 10 imports a minute per user.

tools.name: createReport
tools.title: Create report
tools.description: Creates a report of type SlideDeck, in a folder the user can see when folderId is set. It starts empty, in the look of a saved template from listTemplates when templateId is set, or of another report when templateDeckId is set: its theme, masters and layouts, without its slides. Ask the user which template to use when the organization has company templates. With link, it imports an existing deck instead, with its slides: a PowerPoint file in OneDrive or SharePoint, or a Google Slides presentation, read with the user's own Microsoft or Google account. Rollstack can open only the Google Slides presentations the user picked in Rollstack before, so a link to one they never did answers 422. Over REST, it also imports a PowerPoint (.pptx) file sent as multipart/form-data in the file field, with name and folderId as fields beside it; a report imported from a file is named after it unless name is set. An import answers once the deck is in, which can take a minute for a large one: send an Idempotency-Key (MCP: idempotencyKey) so a retry doesn't import it twice. At most 10 imports a minute per user.

When the client can show one, a view shows the user the slides as the agent drafts them. Without chatId the message starts a new chat, which shows in the user's chat history in the app. With it, the message continues that chat and waits its turn while a reply is still generating. Several chats on a report can generate at once; an agent working on a part of the report another chat is editing works on something else or says so. For slides built from your own data, a connected dashboard, a warehouse table or a spreadsheet, upload the data with createDataset, find the dashboard or Salesforce report with searchDashboards, the Snowflake, Databricks or BigQuery table with searchTables or the spreadsheet with searchSpreadsheets, add any of them with addReportDatasheets and pass the datasheet ids as datasheetIds. For a brief, a report or notes to build from, upload it with createDocument and pass its id in documentIds. Only its editors may. At most 6 messages a minute per user. To write the slides yourself instead, start with getReportDesign.

formula.description: A formula over one source row: ${Column} names a source column or an earlier custom field. No sum(), mean(), min(), max(), median(), count(), offset(), index() or running_total(), which read other rows

__schema13.description: A formula: ${Column} names a dimension or measure by its name before renames; numbers, "text", yes, no, null; + - * / (dividing by 0 gives empty); = != < <= > >=; AND, OR, NOT; if(condition, then, else), coalesce(a, b), round(x, digits), abs(x), concat(a, b), is_null(x), to_string(x); sum(x), mean(x), min(x) and max(x) of a column over the rows shown, after the row limit, such as ${Sales} / sum(${Sales}) for each row's share of the rows shown; offset(x, n), the value n rows below in the rows shown (-1 the row above, empty past the first or last), and index(x, n), the value in row n of the rows shown (counting from 1), such as ${Sales} - offset(${Sales}, 1) for the lead over the next row; median(x), and count(x) of its values that aren't empty, over the rows shown; running_total(x), the sum of x from the first row shown down to this one, in the rows' order; power(x, y), x to the power y (empty for a negative x with a fractional y); diff_days(start, end), the whole days from the start date to the end date, negative when the end is earlier, empty when either is empty

__schema74.description: Rows to keep: a number, an integer parameter, or null for all

__schema77.description: A table's total row, its subtotal rows and, with a split, its Total column, each measure over the rows shown (under a limit, only those). Omit for none

row.description: A last row with the total of each column; charts leave it out

column.description: With a pivot after the aggregate: a Total column with each row across the pivot

__schema85.description: Conditions on the grouped rows' dimensions and measures (by their name before renames), all of which must hold, right after the grouping and before the calculations, the sort and the limit, as SQL's HAVING does, so the calculations and the limit only see the rows kept: each region's share among the regions with more than 20 deals. __schema87.description: Conditions on the grouped rows' dimensions, measures and before-limit calculations (by their name before renames), all of which must hold, after the calculations and before the column order, the sort and the limit, so the limit counts only the rows kept while the calculations still cover every group: the top 10 customers of those over 1,000,000, the regions with over 5% of the total. __schema89.description: Conditions on the rows' own columns (dimensions, measures and calculations by their name before renames), all of which must hold, after the sort, the limit and every calculation: keep the rank 1 row of the top 10, with its share of the 10. To keep rows before the limit, use keepRowsBeforeLimit. Needs a dimension or measure and no split

Copy the shape of the parameter's `value` in `listBursts`, or of a variant's in `listBurstVariants`:

- A list of values: `{ "type": "categorical", "values": ["EMEA"] }`, with at least one value. `operator` can also be `is_not`, `contains` or `doesnt_contain`; it is `is` when left out.

On an older report, `all` emails after every run of the whole report, whether started by a schedule, with `startReportRun` or in the app, and `scheduled` only after runs its schedules start; a run of only some syncs never emails it. With `none` (Manual in the app), no run sends it: the email goes out only when sent with `sendReportEmail` or from the app. Defaults to `all`.

ignoredFailureStatusMessages.description:
The failures that shouldn't stop a run from emailing the report (see `trigger`). A run with failures still sends the email when all of them are in this list. On a slide deck, a run in which every datasheet fails never does. On a slide deck, include `internal_server_error` to email the report even when some of its datasheets fail. On an older report, include the `error.code` values from `listReportSyncs` to ignore. Defaults to `slide_not_found` alone, so by default a slide deck's run with any failed datasheet sends no email, and an older report's run still emails when only syncs on a missing slide fail.

The other values describe why a sync of an older report failed, and have an effect only on older reports:

- `dashboard_not_found`, or the older `tableau_view_not_found`: the dashboard, Tableau workbook, Power BI report or spreadsheet could not be found.
- `dashboard_tab_not_found`: the dashboard tab, Tableau view, Power BI report page or spreadsheet sheet could not be found.
- `dashboard_not_ready`: the dashboard took too long to load.
- `dashboard_has_errors`: the dashboard or spreadsheet failed to load because of an error in the tool it comes from.
- `dashboard_invalid_layout`: the dashboard's layout is invalid, and it needs to be saved again.
- `element_not_found`, or the older `metabase_element_not_found` and `looker_element_not_found`: the visualization could not be found.
- `slide_not_found`, or the older `google_slide_not_found`: the slide that shows the visualization could not be found.
- `file_not_found`: the spreadsheet file the visualization comes from could not be found.
- `sheet_not_found`: the spreadsheet sheet could not be found.
- `sheet_hidden`: the spreadsheet sheet is hidden and needs to be unhidden.
- `range_not_found`: the spreadsheet range could not be found.
- `duplicate_file_failed`: Rollstack could not prepare the spreadsheet file for the update.
- `merged_range_on_filter_range`: the visualization has merged cells, which filters can't be applied to.
- `insufficient_permissions`: the owner doesn't have edit access to the file.
- `image_cropping_failed`: Rollstack could not crop the visualization's image.
- `visualization_not_found`: the visualization could not be found in the dashboard.
- `visualization_not_ready`: the visualization took too long to load.
- `visualization_has_errors`: the visualization failed to load because of an error in the tool it comes from.
- `visualization_empty`, or the older `empty_data`: the visualization is empty.
- `invalid_credentials`: the connection's credentials are invalid.
- `missing_credentials`: the connection's credentials were deleted, or the owner's access to it was suspended.
- `instance_unavailable`: the data source's instance is temporarily unavailable.
- `column_not_found`: a column the native chart uses is missing from its data.
- `fetch_summary_data_error`, `fetch_visual_specification_error`, `missing_data`, `missing_formatted_value` and `viz_not_ready`: Rollstack could not fetch the data of a native chart.
- `incorrect_data_structure`: the native chart's structure doesn't fit its data.
- `malformed_data`: Rollstack could not fetch the data of a native chart or, from Snowflake, Databricks or BigQuery, the query is invalid.
- `worksheet_not_found`: the Tableau worksheet could not be found.
- `sync_not_found`: the visualization was deleted.
- `file_update_failed`: the data was fetched but could not be written into the file.

- `insufficient_permissions`: the owner doesn't have edit access to the file.
- `image_cropping_failed`: Rollstack could not crop the visualization's image.
- `visualization_not_found`: the visualization could not be found in the dashboard.
- `visualization_not_ready`: the visualization took too long to load.
- `visualization_has_errors`: the visualization failed to load because of an error in the tool it comes from.
- `visualization_empty`, or the older `empty_data`: the visualization is empty.
- `invalid_credentials`: the connection's credentials are invalid.
- `missing_credentials`: the connection's credentials were deleted, or the owner's access to it was suspended.
- `instance_unavailable`: the data source's instance is temporarily unavailable.
- `column_not_found`: a column the native chart uses is missing from its data.
- `fetch_summary_data_error`, `fetch_visual_specification_error`, `missing_data`, `missing_formatted_value` and `viz_not_ready`: Rollstack could not fetch the data of a native chart.
- `incorrect_data_structure`: the native chart's structure doesn't fit its data.
- `malformed_data`: Rollstack could not fetch the data of a native chart or, from Snowflake, Databricks or BigQuery, the query is invalid.
- `worksheet_not_found`: the Tableau worksheet could not be found.
- `sync_not_found`: the visualization was deleted.
- `file_update_failed`: the data was fetched but could not be written into the file.

tools.name: searchDashboards
tools.title: Search dashboards
tools.description: The dashboards of a Looker, Metabase, Omni, Lightdash, Sigma, Tableau or Power BI connection whose name holds any word of query or its singular, in any case, at most 50: those the most of the organization's reports read first, copies, old and personal ones last, then most words first, read with the user's access to the connection. A Tableau dashboard is a workbook, its views its tabs; a Power BI one a report, its pages its tabs; a Sigma one a workbook, its pages its tabs. On a Sigma connection, query can be a link to a workbook the user pasted: it finds only that workbook, with the page the link opens on as tabId, but not the link's control values, saved view or tag, and a link to another Sigma organization is rejected. On a Salesforce connection it finds reports the same way, the most recently run first among equals, each with its format: a report has no tabs, so add a tabular or summary one to a report with addReportDatasheets by its reportId, without getDashboard, and tell the user a matrix or joined one can't be added yet. Search by the name the user gives, confirm the dashboard with the user, then check its tabs and charts with getDashboard or add it to a report with addReportDatasheets. listConnections gives the connection's type and id.

type.description: The type of connection, as `type` in `listConnections`: the BI tool it connects to. Only Looker, Metabase, Omni, Lightdash, Sigma, Tableau and Power BI (`PowerBI`) connections have dashboards, and on a `Salesforce` connection the search finds its reports.

id.description: Unique identifier for the connection, from `listConnections`, which also returns its `type`.

params.description: The ids of what the tool acts on

query.description: Options for the call, such as filters, paging or how long to wait

Words to search for in names, separated by spaces: a dashboard, table, model or spreadsheet is returned when its name contains any of them, case-insensitively, a table's full name with its database and schema. If omitted, results aren't filtered by name. At most 50 results are returned either way.

tools.name: getDashboard
tools.title: Get dashboard
tools.description: A dashboard of a Looker, Metabase, Omni, Lightdash, Sigma, Tableau or Power BI connection, read with the user's access to the connection (a Salesforce report has no tabs or charts to read, so add it with addReportDatasheets directly): its tabs, and the charts and filters of the tab tabId names, one of the ids in tabs (else the one the dashboard opens on, a Power BI report's or Sigma workbook's first page). Tableau and Power BI list no charts or filters here: once the tab is added to a report, its charts are listed from its picture for the slides agent to add; a Sigma page lists its charts and tables, and the workbook's controls as its filters. Find the dashboard's id with searchDashboards. Confirm the dashboard and tab with the user, then add it to a report with addReportDatasheets; for another tab, call it again with that tab's id from tabs.
